cases.reason: Whether 'the value of argument-1' is greater than zero is decided by how the argument is evaluated. Argument-1 is an arithmetic expression (15.2 AR9), and under 2002 ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD it is evaluated by standard arithmetic, with each operation truncated to 32 significant digits. That mode has no 2023 counterpart, so the 2023 row cannot witness it. The reader's probes used only data items. Program std_arith.cob (OPTIONS ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, A PIC S9(31) VALUE 1234567890123456789012345678901, EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION checking on, with a declarative) evaluates FUNCTION LOG(A * 100 + 5 - A * 100). Under 2002: the exact sum A*100+5 has 33 digits; truncated to 32 it equals A*100, so the argument value is 0. That makes it an incorrect value, so EC-ARGUMENT-FUNCTION exists and R stays 7. Observed at --std 2002: no exception, 'LOG R=+00001.609437' (that is LOG 5), and COMPUTE R = A*100+5-A*100 shows DIFF=+00005.000000.
